Physics · Electricity, Magnetism & Optics

Trail Technology

An advanced enrichment course. The riding connection is the technology on and around the bike: motors, batteries, lights, sensors, GPS and lenses.

3 units · 11 modules · activities in development

Units

  1. Unit 7 Electricity 5 modules

    Charge, voltage, current, resistance and circuits, through e-bike batteries and bike lights.

    1. Module 1

      Introduction: The Electric Bike

      How mechanics connects to the electrical systems on a modern bike.

      • Identify the electrical systems on a modern bike
      • Trace energy from battery to motor to wheel
      • Connect force, energy and power to their electrical versions
      Activities in development Lesson coming

    2. Module 2

      Electric Charge and Electric Field

      Charge, conductors and insulators, Coulomb’s law and electric fields.

      • Describe positive and negative charge, and conservation of charge
      • Tell conductors and insulators apart
      • Use Coulomb’s law
      • Draw and interpret electric field lines
      Activities in development Lesson coming

    3. Module 3

      Electric Potential and Capacitors

      Voltage as energy per charge, potential energy, equipotentials and capacitors.

      • Explain voltage as energy per unit charge
      • Calculate the energy a battery stores, in joules and watt-hours
      • Calculate capacitance and the energy a capacitor stores
      • Interpret equipotential lines and field strength
      Activities in development Lesson coming

    4. Module 4

      Current, Resistance and Ohm’s Law

      Current, resistance and resistivity, Ohm’s law, electrical power and heating, AC and DC.

      • Calculate current as charge per unit time
      • Use Ohm’s law
      • Calculate electrical power and energy use
      • Explain how material, length and thickness set resistance
      • Tell alternating and direct current apart
      Activities in development Lesson coming

    5. Module 5

      Circuits and DC Instruments

      Series and parallel circuits, voltage drops, internal resistance, meters and capacitors in circuits.

      • Analyze a series circuit
      • Analyze a parallel circuit
      • Explain a battery’s internal resistance and terminal voltage
      • Describe how to measure current and voltage
      • Describe how a capacitor charges and discharges in a circuit
      Activities in development Lesson coming
  2. Unit 8 Magnetism & Wireless Technology 3 modules

    Magnetic fields, motors and generators, and the electromagnetic waves behind GPS and wireless sensors.

    1. Module 6

      Magnetism

      Magnetic poles and fields, the force on a moving charge and on a current, and how motors and sensors use it.

      • Describe magnetic poles and field lines
      • Find the force on a moving charge in a magnetic field
      • Find the force on a current-carrying wire
      • Explain how an electric motor turns current into rotation
      • Explain how a magnet and sensor measure wheel speed
      Activities in development Lesson coming

    2. Module 7

      Electromagnetic Induction

      Magnetic flux, Faraday’s and Lenz’s laws, generators, eddy currents, transformers and AC.

      • Calculate magnetic flux
      • Use Faraday’s law to find an induced emf
      • Use Lenz’s law to find the direction of an induced current
      • Explain how a generator or dynamo makes electricity
      • Describe transformers and AC
      Activities in development Lesson coming

    3. Module 8

      Electromagnetic Waves

      Electromagnetic waves, the spectrum, frequency, wavelength and energy, and how they carry information.

      • Place types of radiation on the electromagnetic spectrum
      • Use c = fλ
      • Explain how radio waves carry signals for GPS and Bluetooth
      • Relate a wave’s frequency to the energy it carries
      Activities in development Lesson coming
  3. Unit 9 Light & Optics 3 modules

    Reflection, refraction and lenses, the eye, and light as a wave.

    1. Module 9

      Geometric Optics

      Reflection, refraction and total internal reflection, mirrors and lenses, focal length, images and magnification.

      • Use the law of reflection
      • Use Snell’s law
      • Explain total internal reflection
      • Use the thin-lens equation to locate an image
      • Calculate magnification
      Activities in development Lesson coming

    2. Module 10

      Vision and Optical Instruments

      The eye as an optical system, accommodation, peripheral vision, corrective lenses and optical instruments.

      • Describe the eye as a lens system
      • Explain how the eye focuses near and far
      • Explain how corrective lenses work
      • Describe how lenses combine in cameras and other instruments
      Activities in development Lesson coming

    3. Module 11

      Wave Optics

      Light as a wave: interference, diffraction, polarization and thin films.

      • Explain constructive and destructive interference of light
      • Describe diffraction patterns
      • Explain polarization and how polarized lenses cut glare
      • Explain thin-film interference in lens coatings
      Activities in development Lesson coming
